description: This Java source file defines the JmsServiceEngine class, which is part of the Apache OFBiz framework. The class handles sending JMS messages through various messaging configurations such as topics, queues, and XA queues. It manages connection setup via JNDI lookups, message creation, and dispatching, integrating with transaction management where applicable.

classes.name: JmsServiceEngine
classes.description: An engine class responsible for managing JMS messaging within the OFBiz framework. It supports sending messages to topics, queues, and XA queues, handling connection setup, message creation, and transaction enlistment.

methods.name: getServiceElement
methods.description: Fetches the JMS service configuration details based on the model service, utilizing the service config utility and handling potential configuration exceptions.

methods.name: makeMessage
methods.description: Creates a JMS MapMessage containing serialized context data and the service invocation name, raising an exception if OUT parameters are required.

methods.name: serverList
methods.description: Determines the list of server configurations to use based on the send mode specified in the service element.

methods.name: runTopic
methods.description: Establishes a JMS topic connection via JNDI, constructs a message, and publishes it to the specified topic.

methods.name: runQueue
methods.description: Establishes a JMS queue connection via JNDI, constructs a message, and sends it to the specified queue.

methods.name: runXaQueue
methods.description: Handles sending JMS messages over XA queues, including transaction enlistment and resource management.

methods.name: run
methods.description: Executes the messaging operations based on the service configuration, iterating over servers of various types.

methods.name: runSync
methods.description: Synchronous execution of the run method, returning the result map.

methods.name: runSyncIgnore
methods.description: Synchronous execution that ignores the output, mainly for fire-and-forget scenarios.

methods.name: runAsync
methods.description: Asynchronously executes the messaging operation and delivers the result to the requester.

methods.name: runAsync
methods.description: Overloaded asynchronous method that runs without passing a requester, executing the messaging independently.
